text:
jess: Heads up — provisioning backlog in us-west-2. Several GPU nodes failing to come up because ephemeral scratch volumes never attach. Noticed a bunch of nvme read-retry entries in dmesg on the affected hosts.
ryan: Pulling logs now from node-ww-045 and node-ww-046. dmesg shows repeated:
```
nvme0: I/O 1234 QID 0 timeout, retrying
nvme0: ctrl reset due to I/O errors
nvme nvme0: aborts and read_retries > 200
```
ryan: iostat shows read latency jumping to 200-300ms and %util pegged.
maya: That matches the provisioning failures — kube attach waits until the disk responds. If controller resets it looks like the attach race fails and the attach plugin aborts.
jess: Any indication whether this is firmware or host-side? Vendor is different across nodes (Mix of vendor-A and vendor-B nvmes).
olivia: Vendor-B reported higher read_retries in their telemetry yesterday in our fleet region. They shipped a firmware with a garbage-collection tweak last month. Could be related.
sahil: Running a quick fio on a spare node returned a high retry count for small-random reads on the controller in question. Profile: `fio --name=randread --ioengine=libaio --rw=randread --bs=4k --numjobs=4 --size=2G` produced occasional timeouts.
ops-oncall: infra-bot alerted 2109990000: [ALERT] nvme_read_retries > 100 on us-west-2-provisioning-pool (incidents suppressed).
infra-bot: [incident] provisioning-delay-detected — 12 pods Pending, 8 nodes with nvme errors.
ryan: Short-term mitigation idea: pause ephemeral-cleaner on the affected AZ to avoid background trim/scrub churn and free up IO for the attach path.
maya: Good call. Also consider bumping kubelet attach timeout to allow controller more retries during transient flaps. But that only masks root cause.
jess: Is there a safe kernel tunable to reduce resets? Maybe reduce aggressive reset/retry behavior. We could try increasing `nvme_core.default_io_timeout` or similar to give drives more time before controller reset.
olivia: Firmware-team suggested trying `nvme_core.default_ps_max_latency_us` for power-state related latencies? Not sure that's relevant. Vendor-B recommended testing with their non-production fw build that delays internal GC during high write windows.
sahil: I don't want to push firmware fleet-wide without a canary. Proposal: pick 2 spare nodes in that AZ, install vendor-B non-prod fw, run a soak with fio + repeated attach/detach cycles, and measure read_retry, reset counts, attach success rate.
jess: Agreed. Meanwhile -- action list: 1) pause ephemeral-cleaner in us-west-2-a and b (ryan) 2) cordon and drain worst nodes to avoid scheduling new GPU pods (maya) 3) start vendor fw canary on 2 spares (olivia) 4) gather full dmesg/iostat/fio artifacts and post link (sahil).
ryan: Paused ephemeral-cleaner for us-west-2-a/b :white_check_mark: Filtering policy set to hold trims and scrubs for 30m.
maya: Cordon/drain started for node-ww-045, keeping existing pods running if possible. Will not evict GPUs mid-job.
ops-oncall: Please keep the oncall loop posted if this starts causing higher preemptions or provisioning timeouts.
olivia: Can we route new provisioning to other regions temporarily (us-east-1) while we stabilize? There's capacity but cross-region provisioning increases cost by ~12% due to inter-region egress and longer scheduling windows.
jess: Yes, let's divert new GPU provisioning to us-east-1 for low-priority batch jobs. Mark high-priority jobs to wait or use dedicated pool.
sahil: Collected fio + dmesg tar for the canary nodes: s3://redwood-diagnostics/us-west-2/nvme-retry/2109990001/ — uploaded. Key findings: read_retries spike correlated with background trim bursts from cleaner prior to pause.
ryan: After pause, observed immediate drop in retry rate on one node but still had occasional spikes on vendor-B machine.
maya: Vendor-B is engaged — they've asked for SMART dumps and controller logs. Olivia, can you coordinate?
olivia: Engaged vendor-B support (case RB-9087). They requested a memory-of-reset dump and a microcode trace. Working with them.
ops-oncall: If vendor can't provide quick patch, fallback plan is to mark vendor-B hardware as "soft-drain" for provisioning and use it only for long-running pre-attached workloads where attach is not required. That reduces immediate failure surface at cost of lowering available ephemeral GPU capacity.
jess: Cost tradeoff noted — soft-draining ~30 nodes costs us ~4% of immediate capacity, but prevents churn and customer impact. Recommend we do that if canary doesn't prove stable in 3 hours. yan: (typo) ryan: re-check: canary started, fio loop includes attach/detach every 60s to mimic kube flow.
sahil: Also noticed kernel `blk_queue_max_hw_sectors` and queue_depth settings differ between vendors; tuning queue_depth downward on vendor-B reduced contention in the canary and lowered retry counts in short-term test. Not a permanent fix.
maya: I'll schedule a controlled rolling policy: 1) 2-hour canary, 2) if stable, roll firmware to an additional 8 nodes, 3) keep ephemeral-cleaner paused during roll. If unstable, soft-drain vendor-B nodes and open a P1 escalation.
jess: Sounds good. Please document any changes in the runbook and ping #incidents if we hit >5% provisioning failures again.
olivia: Uploaded vendor requested logs to support case. Vendor-B replied: "preliminary suspicion: internal GC + host TRIM burst causing controller-side retry storm. We have a microcode candidate but need longer soak."
ops-oncall: Noted next checkpoints: 2109990200 (canary halfway), 2109990520 (end of canary).
ryan: Canary halfway: vendor-A node stable, vendor-B node still showing occasional read_retries but attach succeeded for most cycles.
sahil: Temporary kernel tweak we tested: lower `nr_requests`/queue_depth for the block device in sysfs reduced queuing pressure. Documented commands used in the artifact tar.
maya: Canary end: vendor-B still failing ~1/1000 attach cycles -> not acceptable for high-confidence provisioning.
jess: Outcome: soft-drain vendor-B nodes for provisioning pool, continue firmware soak with vendor, keep ephemeral-cleaner paused for 4h, and schedule a follow-up postmortem if vendor patch doesn't land by EOD.
olivia: Filing runbook updates and scheduling vendor patch rollout timeline.
ops-oncall: Closing incident alert for now, leaving monitoring escalations open for 6h.
infra-bot: [INFO] provisioning-diversion enacted -> batch jobs routing to us-east-1 for low-priority queues.
jess: Thanks team — please paste final artifacts and timeline in the follow-up thread. :thumbsup:"
